title: review: H6 fix round 2: gate() keeps the no-worktree early continue so a done task without a worktree never reaches the tests-green subprocess with None (review T-0377)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain d362503 (T-0359) and abda0dc (T-0373) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Review T-0377 on T-0373, one high finding:
1. orchestrator/daemon.py:782 the refactor of gate()'s worktree guard dropped the early continue for tasks without a worktree; the missing-tests check is now inside if worktree:, but the unconditional subprocess.run([str(merge.TESTS_GREEN), worktree]) after it still runs with worktree None, raising TypeError outside gate()'s per-task try, so one done execute task without a worktree aborts gate() for every tick and starves every other merge and review.
Fix: restore the early continue (or an explicit skip with one stderr line) for tasks whose worktree is falsy or not a directory, before both the missing-tests check and the subprocess; keep the missing-tests branch as it is for tasks with a worktree. Test: tests/test_daemon.py::test_gate_skips_task_without_worktree_and_continues (two done tasks: the first without a worktree, the second with one; gate() gates the second and raises nothing).
Keep the T-0359 and T-0373 tests and every existing test green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0, then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows abda0dc and d362503 below your commit
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
